To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the expressiveness of the three sample systems is not sufficient to support a general purpose software reuse repository, but that (2) the representational capabilities and distribution mechanisms are sufficiently general that they can be used to support the development of a general purpose software repository.

the current state of the art of information retrieval systems is not yet adequate for software reuse repositories, and that the most important research issues for the next generation of repositories are: the development of a standard repository language, the definition of a standard repository query language, and the definition of standard repository query interfaces.
archie, autoLIB, and WAIS are all useful tools, that WAIS is the most useful, that archie is the least useful, and that autoLIB is the best of the three in terms of expressiveness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a repository system which will provide a coherent, integrated, and distributed environment for software reuse.
developing a theoretical foundation for the design and implementation of repositories for software reuse, and with the practical application of this foundation.
how to design and develop repositories for software reuse that can be used by a wide variety of users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of the art is not yet ready for prime-time, but that there is a lot of work in progress, and that the prospects for the future are quite good.
we are still a long way from the ideal repository, but we have a good foundation to work from.
the state of the art in software reuse is not yet ready to be used in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified some of the key issues in the design of a software reuse repository, and have demonstrated some of the ways in which these issues can be addressed.
the current state of the art is not sufficient to support the needs of software reuse repositories.

, while there are a number of issues that need to be resolved before a software reuse repository can be built, the basic technology is available to build such a repository, and the issues are primarily those of implementation, rather than fundamental technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a repository technology must provide for the expression of the following concepts: (1) the ability to represent and retrieve information about software artifacts, such as programs, libraries, and documentation; (2) the ability to express relationships among software artifacts; and (3) the ability to provide a coherent user interface to the repository.
a repository is more than the software that it contains.
the expressiveness of repository technology is not the primary factor in the usefulness of a repository.
